propositions: Detached pytest runs via nohup report errors (failed tests, stderr diagnostics) that do not reproduce when the same commit is run in foreground, creating false positive signals that waste investigator time and erode confidence in the test suite.

The root cause is not detachment itself but concurrent external mutations to the shared checkout (file creation, git operations, process reaping) that happen only during detached runs because foreground runs block the agent; these are misattributed to the test by autouse guards that cannot distinguish internal from external changes.

The _no_repo_root_leaks guard in tests/conftest.py fires on concurrent external top-level file writes, falsely asserting that the test leaked entries, deletes the file, and blames an innocent test whose teardown straddles the external write (deterministically reproduced by concurrent touch during a run).

Browser e2e test failures reported by the guard lack diagnostic context: when a child process is signal-killed (SIGKILL, SIGHUP) by a concurrent external reap, proc.stderr is empty, but the current code never inspects proc.returncode and reports no cause, making a signal death indistinguishable from a product defect.

Detached validation practice is entirely undocumented in docs/local-dev-env.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, AGENTS.md despite being routine for agents, creating uncertainty about whether detached runs are trustworthy and what isolation precautions are required.

The distinction between concurrent external mutations (this ticket) and self-inflicted HEAD moves (the _no_repo_commits sibling guard) must be clearly separated so both classes of misattribution are not conflated into folklore that dismisses real regressions.
